papers.title: Deep Residual Architectures for Automated Chest Radiography in Curated Hospital Archives
papers.dataset: NIH ChestX-ray14 (n = 1,200 curated frontal scans, motion-free)
papers.methodology: Supervised fine-tuning of ResNet-50 with weighted cross-entropy loss
papers.main_conclusion: Deep learning vision backbones reliably match and surpass certified human radiologists on curated thoracic anomalies.

claims.statement: ResNet-50 models demonstrate superior 94.2% sensitivity over human clinician baselines.
claims.verbatim_quote: Our fine-tuned ResNet-50 model achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 94.2% across 1,200 curated frontal views, outperforming senior radiology fellows by 4.8%.

claims.statement: Automated radiography is ready for immediate first-line clinical deployment in triage.
claims.verbatim_quote: The low false-negative rate (2.1%) supports immediate zero-touch triage deployment in emergency departments.

papers.title: In-the-Wild Generalization Collapse of Thoracic Vision Classifiers on Real-World Clinical Data
papers.dataset: West African Tertiary Hospital EMR (n = 3,450 raw clinical X-rays, portable bedside)
papers.methodology: Out-of-distribution evaluation of standard ResNet-50 and ViT models on uncurated bedside radiography
papers.main_conclusion: Standard lab-trained deep learning radiography models collapse severely when deployed on uncurated, portable bedside X-rays with artifact.

claims.statement: ResNet-50 diagnostic accuracy degrades catastrophically to 62.4% in uncurated hospital environments.
claims.verbatim_quote: When evaluated on 3,450 bedside examinations containing rotation and medical hardware artifacts, accuracy plummeted from 93% to 62.4%, falling below clinician performance.

claims.statement: Automated triage without radiologist-in-the-loop is unsafe for patient outcomes.
claims.verbatim_quote: Unsupervised autonomous triage introduces unacceptable diagnostic error rates on out-of-distribution portable acquisitions.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Contrastive Conditioning Restores Clinical Robustness Under Distribution Shift
papers.dataset: Multi-center Cross-Hospital Cohort (n = 5,000 mixed curated and bedside scans)
papers.methodology: Self-supervised domain-invariant contrastive pre-training prior to linear probing
papers.main_conclusion: Contrastive domain adaptation bridges the gap between curated lab benchmarks and messy clinical deployments.

claims.statement: Domain-invariant pre-training recovers 88.7% accuracy across heterogeneous hospital hardware.
claims.verbatim_quote: Domain-adaptive contrastive training stabilized sensitivity at 88.7%, successfully mitigating the distribution collapse observed in standard supervised baselines.

edges.reason_for_difference: Smith et al. tested on high-resolution motion-free lab archives (n=1,200), whereas Adewale et al. evaluated portable bedside radiography with patient motion and medical artifact (n=3,450), causing accuracy to collapse from 94.2% to 62.4%.
edges.source_quote: Our fine-tuned ResNet-50 model achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 94.2% across 1,200 curated frontal views.
edges.target_quote: When evaluated on 3,450 bedside examinations containing rotation artifacts, accuracy plummeted to 62.4%.

edges.reason_for_difference: Smith recommends immediate autonomous triage based on lab data, but Adewale warns that autonomous triage is clinically unsafe due to high false negatives on real hospital data.
edges.source_quote: The low false-negative rate supports immediate zero-touch triage deployment.
edges.target_quote: Unsupervised autonomous triage introduces unacceptable diagnostic error rates on out-of-distribution portable acquisitions.

edges.reason_for_difference: Both studies confirm that standard supervised models fail under distribution shift, and both support the need for robust domain adaptation to handle uncurated clinical data.
edges.source_quote: Accuracy plummeted from 93% to 62.4% on portable bedside X-rays.
edges.target_quote: Domain-adaptive contrastive training stabilized sensitivity at 88.7%, successfully mitigating the distribution collapse.

consensus.executive_summary: The literature exhibits strong consensus that deep learning models achieve high diagnostic fidelity on curated thoracic images, but standard supervised models suffer severe performance degradation (falling to ~62%) when deployed on real-world bedside X-rays with artifact. Recent domain-adaptive contrastive learning bridges this gap, reaching ~88% in uncurated hospital environments.
agreed_findings: Deep learning backbones match or surpass human radiologists on clean, motion-free curated scans.
Standard supervised models suffer distribution collapse on low-quality portable bedside radiography.
Domain-invariant adaptation is necessary before real clinical deployment.
conflicting_findings: Clinical readiness: Whether current models are mature enough for autonomous emergency room triage (Smith argues yes; Adewale argues it is dangerously premature).
consensus.recommended_resolution: Future benchmark evaluations must standardize testing across multi-hospital out-of-distribution portable datasets rather than relying exclusively on curated lab benchmarks like ChestX-ray14.
